newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen - decision Wednesday on Krupp venture.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen - decision Wednesday on Krupp venture.

text.p: German steel companies Thyssen AG and Krupp AG will decide on Wednesday at the latest whether or not to found a joint venture, Thyssen chief executive Dieter Vogel said on Tuesday.
In a German television interview, Vogel also said that the prospects that the companies would agree on a joint venture were good and that they would aim to avoid job losses in any deal.
"By tomorrow evening it will be clear if there will be such a company," Vogel said.
Preserving jobs would be difficult, Vogel said, but he was optimistic.

Thyssen and Krupp announced their intention to explore co-operation possibilities on Monday as Krupp abandoned a hostile takeover bid for its rival which it launched last week to the horror of unions and many politicians.

The companies are now expected to set up a joint venture but no terms of an agreement have been fixed. The venture would be controlled by Thyssen, whose steel activities are larger and In a separate interview, Vogel said a steel industry merger offered better prospects for workers than a hostile takeover by Krupp would have done.
Speaking to WDR television, Vogel said that now the threat of a wholesale takeover was gone, the two companies could work out the details of steel co-operation intensively and soberly.

Despite the abandonment of Krupp's takeover gambit, 30,000 steel workers demonstrated in Germany's financial capital Frankfurt on Tuesday to protest against the power of the banks behind the bid and job losses they still expect to hit them.
But Vogel said that financing an all-out takeover bid would have forced Krupp to raise a massive 15 billion marks in debt.
"The workers would have borne the brunt," Vogel said.
